dod_intent_evidence: USAF SBIR Phase II ($733K, 2022) for blockchain-based aircraft data loading, and site lists 'United States Air Force | Air Guard | Space Force | Department of Defense' as customers with a 'USAF Commander' quote (about page, SBIR record).
score_evidence: Buzzword stacking: 'Artificial Intelligence Generative AI Large Language Models Advanced Cryptography Distributed Ledger Technology Blockchain' and '1,000,000s of datasets verified' → lab_language_intensity

'ADAM de-risks data in real-time, from source to use, across all domains, regardless of connectivity' — connectivity dismissed in one clause, no ATO/RMF/STIG/crypto-cert language anywhere → deployment_awareness_absence (capped: own-language ~683 words)

blind_spots.blind_spot: A distributed ledger promised to work 'regardless of connectivity'
blind_spots.operator_reality: Ledger verification needs node consensus and sync; DDIL comms partition the network first, so 'real-time verification from source to use' fails exactly in the contested environment it's marketed for — same connectivity-assumption failure as the 30fps crowd-detection case
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Tiny team demoing on connected lab networks; blockchain framing predates any austere-site test
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ADAM de-risks data in real-time, from source to use, across all domains, regardless of connectivity.

blind_spots.blind_spot: ECHO edge comms app/hardware with no accreditation or crypto-certification story
blind_spots.operator_reality: Fielding a comms and document-sharing device on government networks in contested environments requires ATO/RMF and certified cryptography; without that, ECHO never leaves the innovation-lab demo table
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their compliance mention is a GSA FASt Lane bullet ('Regulatory Compliance') — acquisition-vehicle compliance, not RMF
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Verified comms and document sharing at the edge. ECHO is the app and hardware your team needs in contested environments.

blind_spots.blind_spot: LLM-based 'trust layer' with no stated impact level or edge-compute footprint
blind_spots.operator_reality: Trident AI has to run somewhere: cloud inference needs IL4/IL5 accreditation, edge inference needs SWaP the aircraft data-loading environment doesn't have; neither path, nor who sustains ledger nodes in the field, is addressed
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product list grew by appending AI buzzwords to a data-integrity core; no ISSO or deployment engineering visible in a 3-person company
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Trident AI is the trust layer that plugs into your existing AI missions.

opener_hook: adamaerocorp.com promises data verification 'regardless of connectivity' — a distributed ledger's consensus is the first thing DDIL comms take away.
what_they_do: 3-4 person, customer-funded shop selling blockchain/ledger data-verification middleware (plus an edge comms app and AI trust layer) for aircraft and space data, reached via SBIR and direct-award vehicles.
